source: Written for KIMO by Claude, 2026-10-07. Kid-friendly meanings; review before relying on them.

terms.meaning: The screen that shows you pictures and words from the computer.
terms.example: I looked at the monitor to see my drawing.

terms.meaning: Buttons with letters and numbers that you press to type.
terms.example: I typed my name on the keyboard.

terms.meaning: You move it and click it to point at things on the screen.
terms.example: I clicked on the game with the mouse.

terms.meaning: It lets the computer play sounds out loud.
terms.example: The music came out of the speaker.

terms.meaning: It picks up your voice so the computer can hear you.
terms.example: I said hello into the microphone.

terms.meaning: A small camera on a computer, so people can see you on a video call.
terms.example: Grandma saw me on the webcam.

terms.meaning: It puts words and pictures from the computer onto paper.
terms.example: The printer printed my party invitation.

terms.meaning: A computer you can fold shut and carry around.
terms.example: Dad took his laptop on the train.

terms.meaning: A flat computer you use by touching the screen, like an iPad.
terms.example: I read a story on my tablet.

terms.meaning: You wear them over your ears to hear sound without anyone else hearing.
terms.example: I wore headphones so I didn't wake the baby.

terms.meaning: A cable that puts power back into a battery.
terms.example: My tablet was flat, so I plugged in the charger.

extra.prompt: Which one do you use to type words?
extra.why: A keyboard has the letters on it.

extra.prompt: Which one lets the computer hear you?
extra.why: A microphone picks up sound, like your voice.

extra.prompt: Which one puts your picture on paper?
extra.why: A printer prints onto paper.

terms.meaning: The "brain" of the computer. It follows instructions super fast.
terms.example: The processor works out the answers to my sums.

terms.meaning: The computer's short-term memory. It holds what you're doing right now and is wiped clean when you switch off.
terms.example: The game was loaded into RAM while I played.

terms.meaning: Where files are kept for a long time, even when the computer is switched off.
terms.example: My photos are kept in storage.

terms.meaning: It stores electricity so a laptop or tablet works without being plugged in.
terms.example: The battery was at 10%, so I charged it.

terms.meaning: A small thing you plug in to carry files from one computer to another.
terms.example: I took my project to school on a USB stick.

terms.meaning: A part that puts information INTO the computer, like a keyboard or mouse.
terms.example: A microphone is an input device.

terms.meaning: A part the computer uses to give information OUT, like a screen or speaker.
terms.example: A printer is an output device.

terms.meaning: Information, like numbers, words, pictures and sounds.
terms.example: The computer saved the data from our class survey.

terms.meaning: One saved piece of work, like a story, a picture or a song.
terms.example: I opened the file with my story in it.

terms.meaning: A place to keep files together so they are tidy and easy to find.
terms.example: I put all my pictures in one folder.

extra.prompt: Is a keyboard an input or an output device?
extra.why: You put letters INTO the computer with a keyboard.

extra.prompt: Is a mouse an input or an output device?
extra.why: You tell the computer where to point with a mouse — that goes IN.

extra.prompt: Is a monitor an input or an output device?
extra.why: The monitor shows you things — information coming OUT.

extra.prompt: Is a speaker an input or an output device?
extra.why: Sound comes OUT of a speaker.

extra.prompt: Is a microphone an input or an output device?
extra.why: Your voice goes IN through the microphone.

extra.prompt: Is a printer an input or an output device?
extra.why: The printer gives you paper OUT of the computer.

extra.prompt: What happens to what's in RAM when you switch the computer off?
extra.why: RAM is short-term memory — it forgets when the power goes off.

extra.prompt: Where should your story be saved so it's still there tomorrow?
extra.why: Storage keeps files even when the computer is off.

terms.meaning: The parts of a computer that you can touch.
terms.example: The keyboard and the screen are hardware.

terms.meaning: The programs and apps that tell a computer what to do. You can't touch software.
terms.example: Games and drawing apps are software.

terms.meaning: A program that does one job, like a game or a camera, often on a phone or tablet.
terms.example: I opened the drawing app.

terms.meaning: The main software that runs the whole computer, like Windows or iPadOS.
terms.example: The operating system starts when you switch the computer on.

terms.meaning: A small picture you tap or click to open something.
terms.example: I tapped the camera icon.

terms.meaning: The arrow or flashing line that shows where you are on the screen.
terms.example: The cursor blinked where my next letter would go.

terms.meaning: Pressing the mouse button once.
terms.example: Click the green button to start.

terms.meaning: Pressing the mouse button twice, quickly, to open something.
terms.example: Double-click the folder to open it.

terms.meaning: Holding down on something and moving it to a new place.
terms.example: I dragged the picture into the folder.

terms.meaning: Keeping your work so you can open it again later.
terms.example: Save your story before you close it.

terms.meaning: A secret word that keeps your account safe. Never share it with friends.
terms.example: I typed my password to get in.

terms.meaning: Typing your username and password to get into your account.
terms.example: I logged in to my school account.

terms.meaning: A new version of software that fixes problems or adds new things.
terms.example: The tablet did an update last night.

extra.prompt: Is a keyboard hardware or software?
extra.why: You can touch a keyboard, so it's hardware.

extra.prompt: Is a game app hardware or software?
extra.why: An app is instructions — you can't touch it, so it's software.

extra.prompt: Who can you share your password with?
options: a grown-up at home who looks after you
extra.why: Passwords are secret. Only a grown-up who looks after you should know it.

terms.meaning: A list of step-by-step instructions to do a job or solve a problem.
terms.example: Our algorithm for making toast had five steps.

terms.meaning: One step that tells someone or something exactly what to do.
terms.example: "Move 10 steps" is an instruction.

terms.meaning: Doing instructions in the right order, one after another.
terms.example: Socks first, then shoes — the sequence matters!

terms.meaning: Instructions written in a language a computer understands.
terms.example: We wrote code to make the cat dance.

terms.meaning: A finished set of code that a computer runs to do a job.
terms.example: I wrote a program that draws a square.

terms.meaning: A person who writes code.
terms.example: When I grow up I want to be a programmer.

terms.meaning: A mistake in a program that stops it working properly.
terms.example: There was a bug, so the cat walked off the screen.

terms.meaning: Finding and fixing the mistakes in a program.
terms.example: We debugged our game until it worked.

terms.meaning: Part of a program that repeats instructions again and again.
terms.example: I used a loop to make the cat jump 10 times.

terms.meaning: A character or object that moves around in a game or in Scratch.
terms.example: My sprite is a flying dragon.

terms.meaning: Starting a program so the computer follows its instructions.
terms.example: Press the green flag to run the program.

extra.prompt: A program that says "Hello" 10 times would use a…
extra.why: A loop repeats instructions, so you don't write them 10 times.

extra.prompt: Your game stops working because of a mistake in the code. The mistake is a…
extra.why: A mistake in a program is called a bug.

extra.prompt: Putting on socks, then shoes, then tying the laces is an example of a…
extra.why: Doing steps in the right order is a sequence.

extra.prompt: You find and fix the mistakes in your game. You are…
extra.why: Finding and fixing mistakes is debugging.

terms.meaning: A named box in a program that stores a value, like a score, which can change.
terms.example: The variable called score went up by 1.

terms.meaning: A question in a program that is either true or false, like "Is the score 10?"
terms.example: The condition checked if the cat touched the wall.

terms.meaning: Code that only runs IF a condition is true.
terms.example: If it is raining, then take an umbrella.

terms.meaning: What the program does when the condition is NOT true.
terms.example: If it is sunny wear a hat, else wear a coat.

terms.meaning: Something that happens, like a click or a key press, that starts some code.
terms.example: Clicking the green flag is an event.

terms.meaning: A named set of instructions you can use again and again just by using its name.
terms.example: I made a function called drawSquare.

terms.meaning: Breaking a big problem into smaller parts that are easier to solve.
terms.example: We decomposed the game into the player, the enemies and the score.

terms.meaning: Something that repeats or is the same, which can help you solve problems.
terms.example: I spotted a pattern: every second tile was red.

terms.meaning: When the computer picks a number or a choice by chance, like rolling a dice.
terms.example: The apple appears in a random place.

terms.meaning: A value that can only be true or false.
terms.example: "Game over" is either true or false.

extra.prompt: A game keeps track of your points in a…
extra.why: A variable stores a value that can change, like a score.

extra.prompt: "When the green flag is clicked" starts the program. The click is an…
extra.why: Something that happens and starts code is an event.

extra.prompt: "If it is raining, take an umbrella." What is the condition?
extra.why: The condition is the true-or-false part: is it raining?

extra.prompt: Splitting "make a game" into "draw the player", "make it move" and "add a score" is called…
extra.why: Breaking a big problem into smaller parts is decomposing.

terms.meaning: Millions of computers all over the world, joined together.
terms.example: I found a video about sharks on the internet.

terms.meaning: A group of computers connected so they can share information.
terms.example: All the computers at school are on one network.

terms.meaning: A way of connecting to the internet without wires.
terms.example: The tablet joined the Wi-Fi at Grandma's house.

terms.meaning: The box at home that connects your devices to the internet.
terms.example: The router has little flashing lights.

terms.meaning: Pages of information on the internet that you can visit.
terms.example: The school has a website with photos of our trip.

terms.meaning: The app you use to look at websites, like Safari or Chrome.
terms.example: I opened the web browser to look at the website.

terms.meaning: A website that helps you find things on the internet, like Google.
terms.example: I used a search engine to find facts about volcanoes.

terms.meaning: Words or a picture you click to go to another page.
terms.example: Click the link to see the next page.

terms.meaning: Copying something from the internet onto your device.
terms.example: I downloaded a new book onto my tablet.

terms.meaning: Sending something from your device up to the internet.
terms.example: Mum uploaded the photos to the cloud.

terms.meaning: A message sent from one person to another over the internet.
terms.example: I sent my teacher an email.

terms.meaning: Keeping your files on the internet, not just on your own device.
terms.example: My photos are saved in the cloud.

terms.meaning: A harmful program that can damage a computer or steal information.
terms.example: Don't open strange emails — they might have a virus.

terms.meaning: Things like your full name, address, school and passwords. Keep them private online.
terms.example: I never put my personal information in a game chat.

extra.prompt: Someone in a game chat asks where you live. What should you do?
options: Don't tell them, and tell a grown-up
extra.why: Your address is personal information. Keep it private and tell a grown-up.

extra.prompt: Someone online you don't know asks for your password. What do you do?
options: Don't share it, and tell a grown-up
extra.why: Never share your password online.

extra.prompt: Moving a photo from your iPad onto the internet is…
extra.why: Sending something UP from your device is uploading.

extra.prompt: Getting a game from the internet onto your iPad is…
extra.why: Bringing something DOWN onto your device is downloading.
